note: Re-judged 2026-10-31 at HEAD 137c2dcfcf by an auditor who did not author dfe4e3aa8d. RFC 5036 Section 3.3: "Upon receipt of an unknown TLV, if U is clear (=0), a notification MUST be returned to the message originator and the entire message MUST be ignored; if U is set (=1), the unknown TLV MUST be silently ignored and the rest of the message processed as if the unknown TLV did not exist." dfe4e3aa8d replaced errors.As into an otherwise unused *unknownTLVError with errors.AsType[*unknownTLVError], the same assertion over the same DecodeInit input. TestLDPInitUnknownTLVUClearNotifies: an Initialization whose second TLV is an unregistered type with U=0; DecodeInit must refuse with unknownTLVError, processMessages must answer an Unknown TLV Notification referring to message 7 of type Initialization, return nil, and leave the session in OpenSent, which is both clauses of the U=0 half (notification to the originator, whole message ignored). TestRFC5036UnknownTLVWithUBitClearIsRefused: the U=0 half on a Label Mapping, Notification refers to it, mapping not applied, session up. TestRFC5036UnknownTLVWithUBitSetIsSkipped (positive): U=1 unknown TLV skipped, mapping applied, nothing written. Re-probed at HEAD by go -overlay of skipTLV (tree untouched): skipping every unknown TLV whatever its U bit reddens both U=0 tests and leaves the positive green; refusing a U=1 unknown TLV reddens only the positive. That is a semantic break of the U-bit decision, stronger than the panic-body revert records on file. Not tagged here: the U=1 half on an Initialization is left to TestRFC5561UnknownCapabilityWithUBitSetIsIgnored, so the U=1 clause is proven on Label Mapping only through this row's tags.
